truthAudit.Summary: Run 2 found 10 of 20 true vulnerabilities. It correctly identified format-string injection, command injection (admin exec variant, not config validation variant), stack buffer overflow, race condition in counter, hardcoded credentials, path traversal, weak PRNG, and division-by-zero. It missed 10 vulnerabilities: integer overflow in factorial, use-after-free in memory-pool cleanup, command injection via config validation, logic bomb in authentication, thread-unsafe timestamp cache, insecure temp file handling, persistent auth state, unhandled exception in variable parsing, integer underflow in memory-pool block split, unbounded parser recursion, data race in result cache, and TOCTOU in config loading. Severity was misclassified for format-string (High vs Critical) and weak PRNG (Low vs High).

Items.Notes: Run 2 explicitly identified the format-string vulnerability in log_debug_message at line 238 with the exact evidence quote matching the truth anchor printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input). The finding title 'Format String Vulnerability in Log Function' and CWE-134 match the truth item.
Run 2 did not mention integer overflow in the factorial computation (result *= i in the fact lambda at lines 315-318). No finding addresses this vulnerability.

Run 2 did not identify the use-after-free in stage_deferred_history_flush where scratch memory allocated from g_memory_pool is used in async tasks after g_memory_pool.cleanup() is called in cleanup().
Run 2 found command injection via admin exec but missed the command injection via config validation (validator_cmd + ' ' + config_file; system(command.c_str()) in validate_config at lines 564-568).
Run 2 identified the inverted bounds check in evaluate_expression that uses strcpy into input_buffer_ when expression length >= sizeof(input_buffer_), matching the truth anchor strcpy(input_buffer_.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: long long old_value = value_; std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_); value_ = old_value + 1;
Items.Notes: Run 2 explicitly identified the race condition in ThreadSafeCounter::increment with the exact evidence quote matching the truth anchors volatile long long, old_value = value_, lock_guard, value_ = old_value + 1.
Run 2 did not identify the logic bomb in authentication where login_attempts_ > 5 combined with EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE sets authenticated_ = true bypassing normal auth.
Run 2 identified path traversal in ConfigLoader::load_config with the exact evidence quote matching the truth anchor config_dir_ + filename.
Run 2 identified buffer overflow in ExpressionParser::parse via strcpy into expression_buffer_ (allocated with 256 bytes) without length check, matching truth anchor strcpy(expression_buffer_.
Run 2 explicitly identified hardcoded admin credentials with the exact evidence quote matching both ADMIN_SECRET and SC_ENT_2025_AUTH anchors.
Run 2 identified weak session token generation using uniform_int_distribution with range 1000-9999, matching truth anchors std::mt19937, uniform_int_distribution, 1000, 9999.
Run 2 did not identify the thread-unsafe static std::tm cached_time in log_debug_message that uses localtime without synchronization.
Run 2 did not identify insecure temporary file handling in append_override_audit_event using TEMP/TMPDIR env vars and system() to write supercalc_emergency.log.
Run 2 did not identify persistent authentication state where authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_ persist across the session without proper lifecycle management.
Run 2 did not identify unhandled exception in handle_variable_command where std::stod(tokens[3]) can throw if tokens[3] is not a valid number.
Run 2 did not identify integer underflow in MemoryPool::allocate where previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES can underflow when previous_size is small.
Run 2 did not identify unbounded recursion in parse_expression calling parse_factor which can call parse_expression again on PAREN_OPEN without depth limit.
Run 2 did not identify data race in result_cache_ where evaluate_cached accesses result_cache_ without cache_mutex_ lock, especially when called from thread_pool_->enqueue.
Run 2 did not identify TOCTOU race in ConfigLoader::load_config between std::filesystem::exists check and subsequent std::ifstream file open, with sleep_for in between.
Run 2 explicitly identified integer division by zero in calculate_route_score with the exact evidence quote matching the truth anchor 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length).
